scope: Immutable source review supplement to test-wait-operational-basis.json. All 75 embedded-program rows have a causal role and missing-counter boundary; 16 additional source reviews cover 29 imported/helper/race/control rows. Counts and inferred control flow are not interchangeable. This is not completion of every native-minimum or tier criterion.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: fakeNative writes one byte before each 1 ms await, optionally appends a newline, then awaits 10 ms before native exit. Terminated and unterminated cases assert complete result, code 1 and natural close; consumer rejection can stop a later child early.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: Native pipe fragmentation, final receipt and EOF must remain; these fixtures do not establish a universal smallest per-byte gap.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: The separate child observations now measure the two terminated/unterminated cases. Success, consumer-rejection and missing-result callers remain unmeasured; do not extrapolate their counts or termination behavior.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The child writes initial JSON immediately and schedules final unterminated JSON after 150 ms. The consumer throws early; assertions require the late native EOF receipt and unknown missing usage.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: 150 ms deliberately places output after early consumer failure; no mathematical minimum or callback latency is established by the passing parent.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: One selected ordinary-child case can observe the original timer handle/callback and report through a permitted sidecar; preserve exact protocol bytes.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: toolEventSeen samples its marker at 20 ms for at most 500 attempts. argvAgent hang mode schedules exit at 30000 ms; claudeAgent protocol hang mode schedules that exit for each matching message. The parent invokes runner contract suites and checks their native exit and expected six passing cases per runner.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: The 20 ms value is a sampling cadence. The 30000 ms timers keep cancellation/deadline fixtures pending; parent success does not mean those deadlines fired or were awaited in full.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Counts require nested contract-child mode/message attribution and original timer handles. Parent test-count assertions do not expose leaf callbacks.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: Every data chunk is appended, stdout is paused and a 2 ms callback resumes it. Close produces the original byte count, tail, SHA256 and chunk count. The selected case requires the complete human response.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: Two milliseconds supplies delayed consumption, not a proven universal minimum. Preserve a native paused pipe and complete byte/hash/EOF assertions.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: One selected ordinary consumer can publish aggregate callback counters with its existing receipt only if every original field/assertion stays intact; chunk count alone counts registrations, not completed resume callbacks.

embeddedGroups.role: external condition polling in a child
embeddedGroups.causalBasis: 12 holds an in-flight MCP tool until pending-release; 95 holds CLI exit while the actual server drains/reserves a root; 423 and 424 hold maintenance readers before live config/filter edits; 425 holds only the first serialized maintenance command; 465 holds sync until the external release file. Native markers/readiness precede the parent operation and actual exit/output follows release.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: Five or ten milliseconds is a predicate sampling cadence, not an unconditional minimum. Poll counts may be zero after the first condition check. Preserve actual process/config/snapshot/reservation ordering.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: These workers have explicit writable bindings or protocol outputs. Exact counters need an observer within existing authority and unchanged output or an external observer; do not add writable files/FDs or alter parser assertions.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The /navigate route schedules location.assign(/denied) at 50 ms. The actual browser interception must refuse main-frame navigation to a robots-denied destination.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: 50 ms makes navigation asynchronous after initial HTML. Host logical time alone does not exercise Chrome request interception; native-equivalence and numeric minimum remain unproved.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: A selected native browser observer could count the actual callback without replacing it, using the existing browser harness. Current parent receipt is not page timer telemetry.

embeddedGroups.role: SDK protocol watchdog and exit delay
embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The installed SDK fixture schedules a 20000 ms failure exit, exchanges actual hook protocol frames, sends result then awaits 10 ms before exit 0. Two cases assert real state-room hook propagation and result text.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: The watchdog is a failure ceiling. The post-result 10 ms is an exit delay; backend teardown after result may prevent completion, so do not infer two completed delays from two successful results.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Instrumented child registration/exit snapshot would need to preserve the SDK worker protocol and authority. No successful-result assertion proves natural child exit here.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The opaque-origin REPORT helper waits in 25 ms steps for both connect-src and img-src violation evidence, with a 10000 ms failure cap. It is distinct from the parent 1500 ms negative escape window.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: Condition completion, not a mandatory 25 ms floor. Native CSP violation delivery and opaque origin remain required.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Embedded browser callback count remains unobserved. A qualified native page observer must preserve report contents, origin and sandbox behavior; no need to repeat the parent negative window solely for this row.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The child wrapper waits synchronously at 1 ms for the actual closed-stdin marker before returning the real execFile handle. The shell closes stdin, touches the marker, waits 50 ms and emits the late hook response. Assertions retain fallback, closed-before-delivery and actual hook result.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: The 1 ms is condition polling; the 50 ms separates native EPIPE/fallback from late response. Source establishes ordering, not a universal smallest delay.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: The ordinary wrapper can count sleepSync iterations without altering its original return/callbacks. Exact shell sleep elapsed requires host observation or a separately reviewed shell diagnostic; do not replace the shell.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The first CLI index execution awaits 30 ms then prints {}. Three simultaneous HTTP retries must all succeed while the calls file records exactly add,index; later failure and retry use rewritten binaries without this delay.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: A deliberate overlap opportunity tests coalescing, not a product deadline. The passing call list infers one completed 30 ms fixture path, not measured elapsed.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: One selected caller can instrument the existing child with authority-preserving telemetry. Do not add fields to the calls.jsonl array oracle or change JSON stdout.

embeddedGroups.role: native completion after broken output sink
embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The child prints start, awaits 50 ms, writes the finished marker, prints end and exits 7. The sink throws; recorded finish must observe the marker, end text, code 7 and closed recorder.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: The 50 ms separates sink failure from child completion; the exact causal marker/native exit is required. One successful selected path infers one completed delay, not measured duration.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: One selected ordinary child can carry lexical timing through a permitted sidecar without touching original stdout, exit or marker assertions; authority must be verified first.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: 361 aborts scratch prune; 362 app.close kills an in-flight boot prune; 363 helper teardown reaps before state removal; 383 aborts the whole maintenance worker; 586 signals the test wrapper after atomic PID publication. Delays of 60000 or 20000 ms keep the original child alive until real cancellation/reaping.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: These are fixture lifetime ceilings, not successfully completed waits. PID/marker publication may precede scheduling, so neither timer entry nor a completed duration follows from readiness alone.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Actual entered delay and cancellation age need child telemetry available before termination or external tracing. An exit-only hook cannot recover SIGKILL observations; keep this explicit rather than inventing completed waits.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The prepared CLI awaits 700 ms only for index, then prints {}. The parent requests refresh, observes a real index PID and closes the app; PID absence and an empty writer gate prove drain.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: The deliberate operation delay exposes closing during refresh. PID visibility does not prove the sleep began, and drain can be cancellation; no completed 700 ms inference.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: The six-caller host-process supplement measures parent polling only. Exact index registration/completion remains nested and requires a worker-authority-preserving observer.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: 562 launches two children, each watching for the other marker and clearing a 1500 ms failure timer on completion. 730 keeps the running sibling alive with a 60000 ms interval, then SIGTERM writes stopped and clears the interval.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: Failure ceiling and live-handle fixture respectively; neither requests a completed 1500/60000 ms wait. Both require actual concurrent child processes and termination.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Ordinary child original-handle observers can measure registration, clear and callback counts through existing permissible telemetry; selected cases are inexpensive. Preserve all original marker and exit assertions.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The generated Node child connects to the host Unix socket, exits 41 on connect, 0 on error and 42 on a 1000 ms deadline. Parent records native code and listener hits.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: 1000 ms is an unsuccessful socket-attempt ceiling; the intended refusal path completes on a native error. No successful minimum applies to the watchdog.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Actual timer registration/clear/end state is unobserved inside the governed worker. Any observer must preserve socket authority and native endpoint; parent no-hit proof is separate.

embeddedGroups.role: Pi forged output and descendant lifetime
embeddedGroups.causalBasis: forge_worker emits forged RPC or overflow then waits 100 ms before returning. linger_worker spawns bash with sleep 60 and then awaits 60000 ms before a late result. Native refusal/cancellation may terminate either path early.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: 100 ms is a late-tool completion opportunity; 60 s holds live native descendants. Passing cancellation does not mean either delay completed.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Per-mode entry and lifecycle need allowed pre-termination telemetry. Original protocol streams and descendant authority must stay unchanged; the parent host sidecar does not count nested workers.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: Shell fixtures retain real sleeping children: runtime probe ignores TERM during sleep 8; version probes use exec sleep 8 or sleep 5; boot probes include failing/no-op/held killer branches and inherited pipes; wrapper cases retain sleep 300 descendants. Row690 also has an unconditional 0.3 s step before failed or timed-out branches.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: These durations retain the native process across production deadlines or cancellation. Do not sum them as completed cost. The 5 s exit/deadline race intentionally admits either outcome; killer readiness and pipe drain are separate guarantees.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Native lifetime and syscall entry require external process observation or reviewed diagnostics. #1933 feasibility/#1939 and #1937 own boot primary-clock/cleanup work; no prototype is treated as delivered. The helper378 supplement measures only host PID polling.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: 610 and 611 wait 0.3 s before writing 8 MiB or 1 MiB after the SDK result; 612 fills first, waits 0.3 s and returns while host cancellation competes. Assertions distinguish state-exceeded, success and cancellation precedence.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: These are deliberate ordering opportunities around real tmpfs writes/monitoring. Native write failure and post-result outcome precedence cannot be established by an isolated host clock jump. Numeric minimum remains unproved.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Shell entry/exit telemetry is missing. Preserve mounts, native monitor cadence and outcome assertions; changing shell output or granting write paths would change the fixture.

embeddedGroups.role: native process hold until explicit kill
embeddedGroups.causalBasis: 613 launches a shell loop before the worker-start callback throws and requires SIGKILL/reaping plus reservation release. 670 has a TERM-ignoring shell loop before direct forced kill. 688 keeps a scope restart worker alive after its note until real restart cleanup.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: Loop cadences keep native processes live; no full interval is a required successful delay. A launch callback or ready marker can precede the first sleep.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Exact shell loop counts and killed syscall ages remain unobserved. Native PID/exit/recovery proof exists independently; external observation would require validating unchanged authority and ptrace effects.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The shell launches a real allocation child, reports its exit, sleeps 2 s then exits 137. This is inside the selected native cgroup probe; the parent-observed sampler interval is a different source row.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: The 2 s is fixture lifetime after allocation, not the observed parent sampler cost. OOM may kill the shell or descendant earlier.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Selected cgroup parent proof does not count shell sleep entry/completion. Exact nested attribution needs a cgroup-safe observer; preserve actual scoped UID/network namespace/capability receipts.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The governed reader publishes readiness and polls at 10 ms for writer-done, while the governed writer polls for reader-ready before creating protected config and completion. Both cap at 200 attempts and retain native exit/output assertions.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: Condition polling with a nominal 2000 ms failure horizon; neither loop requires 200 iterations or a positive minimum.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Exact shell iterations are absent. Existing governed workers cannot gain writable sidecars or extra descriptors; an external observer must be proven non-invasive before using counters.

embeddedGroups.role: native exit after two output streams
embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The shell prints version and diagnostic, sleeps 20 ms then exits 3. The caller asserts both complete outputs, exit 3, the actual production deadline cleared and no later unhandled rejection.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: 20 ms separates output from exit, not a public deadline; one successful branch infers the sleep completed without supplying elapsed telemetry.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Exact shell elapsed remains missing. Parent timer lifecycle observations concern the deadline, not this shell delay.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: 678 fills one real tmpfs, holds it with sleep 1 while another mount is checked, then awaits exit. 679 deliberately holds a fake launcher before pivot with sleep 6 under an outer tmpfs so the held-root gate must refuse.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: The first delay retains overlap for independent mount proof. The second is a refused launcher lifetime; do not count six seconds from the literal. Neither establishes a universal minimum.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Actual shell telemetry missing. Row679 retains original location-sensitive failure and faithful non-/tmp control under #1931; a green control does not erase the failed context.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: A shell appends a byte then sleeps 20 ms repeatedly while the real adapter is running. Scope tests freeze at the cap, retain a native negative observation, grant once, refuse a second grant and Stop; Pi voice refuses before worker admission.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: 20 ms is a write cadence, not the negative observation duration. Native freezer/writer behavior is required; no source inference of exact callback/iteration count from unchanged bytes.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Exact shell iterations/frozen syscall states are missing. Existing parent heartbeat snapshots establish native change/absence only at their capture boundaries, not a completed-sleep census.

embeddedGroups.role: native tmpfs contention and late mutations
embeddedGroups.causalBasis: 689 writes 1 MiB then sleeps 200 ms repeatedly; 710 appends state then sleeps 1 s; 711 holds for 2 s before append; 712 starts a 200 ms late symlink swap while the main shell holds 500 ms; 713 performs tmpfs work then sleeps 1 s before append; 714 holds a crash worker for 30 s. Parent source review maps each scenario and native assertions.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: These are overlapping fixture holds, write cadence and delayed mutation, not a sum of waited literals. The scope 200 ms negative check equals its shell cadence with zero nominal extra allowance; no guaranteed numeric sensitivity is claimed.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Exact shell counts/elapsed remain missing despite passing parent scenarios. Original tmpfs/mount/process authority and independent final bytes must remain; source-derived path counts are not timer telemetry.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: Malformed readiness controls (empty, wrong, missing) print a diagnostic then enter an indefinite Atomics.wait while the parent must reject by its deadline and reap the child.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: Indefinite hold is a fixture lifetime, not an elapsed minimum. Parent seeing a file/diagnostic does not prove the subsequent Atomics call was entered.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Entry requires observation before blocking; exit-sidecar telemetry cannot run while blocked or after SIGKILL. Preserve exact readiness/stdout/stderr oracles.

embeddedGroups.role: native operation completion and cancellation ordering
embeddedGroups.causalBasis: 693 delays real Git by 600 ms for during/after cancellation; 694 touches probe-started, sleeps 300 ms, touches probe-finished and exits success/refusal before app resources may open; 696 sleeps 200 ms then prints after cancelling stdout or stderr, and preserves exit status/gate reuse.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: These delays expose asynchronous preparation or completion. Some cancellation paths may terminate before sleep completion; successful probe-finished or exit 0 paths can infer completion, not elapsed. Numeric minimum/equivalence remains unproved.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Shell exact entry/completion counters are absent. Preserve actual Git, resource-opening assertions and both stream-cancellation variants. Parent case wall is not leaf delay cost.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The descendant samples parent PID liveness every 20 ms, then attempts mirror poisoning. Namespace init must reap it before credentialed transport; the parent retains a separate 1100 ms negative check and remote-content assertions.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: 20 ms is predicate cadence, not the 1100 ms security window. Native namespace descendant lifetime and host storage validation remain essential.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Exact shell loop/entry count absent. Source construction alone does not prove the loop ran before namespace teardown; do not grant it telemetry write permissions.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: Each governed-lock actor first appends start, writes/adds its note, sleeps 200 ms only if git add succeeds, commits, and appends end. Script selection is scenario- and actor-step-specific.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: 200 ms widens overlap inside native Git work; it is not a product deadline. Exact actor event order/commit proof is separate from elapsed minimum.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Host-side policy probe telemetry does not count shell callbacks. Retain both actors, actual Git lock, credential boundary and original event stream; external observation would need separate validation.

embeddedGroups.causalBasis: 718 ignores TERM and holds an owned process with a 1000 ms interval; 719 keeps a socket/60000 ms interval live during ordinary CLI output; 720 holds an embedding lock before SIGKILL; 724 holds search CLI during abort/deadline/HTTP disconnect (already-aborted branch never launches); 728 adds a 1000 ms interval only for server role after filesystem checks; 731 holds writable FD/mmap donor authority with a 60000 ms interval.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: Intervals retain process lifetime, not mandatory callback opportunities. A prior ready write can precede registration; no fired-count inference from publication. Real exit/kill/socket/lock/authority proof remains.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Exact registration/fired/clear data absent inside each generated child. Ordinary children can sometimes publish lifecycle telemetry, but worker/donor authority must not expand and SIGKILL cannot supply an exit snapshot.

embeddedGroups.role: native frame after opaque preview scroll
embeddedGroups.causalBasis: The embedded preview handles scroll-preview-to-end, scrolls to document end and schedules report in requestAnimationFrame. Parent accepts only the expected source/origin, observes scrolled top, then tests fresh destination press/reload with the same iframe and top reset.
embeddedGroups.elapsedMinimumDisposition: One native frame opportunity after scroll is the causal unit, not a fixed millisecond floor. Retain all three pointer projects and real iframe/input behavior.
embeddedGroups.missingCounterEvidence: Exact callback count is not retained in existing trace. A selected browser observer can count without replacing rAF; do not substitute corrected-source paint proof for frozen04a timer telemetry.

writeFileSync(binary, `#!/bin/sh
if [ "$1" = "--version" ]; then exit 0; fi

observationPointRules: A published marker can precede timer or Atomics entry.
A passing parent command is not a nested callback count.
Fixture lifetimes and failure ceilings are not completed elapsed waits.
Condition samplers need actual iteration counts; a reached loop can execute zero times.
A native opportunity or source allowance does not prove the smallest reliable window.
Do not add writable bindings, inherited FDs, altered protocol output or relaxed assertions solely to collect counters.
interpretation: The historical operational classifications remain as originally published. New selected observations and recovered traces apply only to their named cases/source. Missing child telemetry does not imply zero; numeric minima are inapplicable to pure logical declarations and denied control inputs, while native absence/late-effect windows retain unresolved equivalence requirements.
